subject.title: fix: CLI timeout warnings explain stopped work

question: Should active CLI turns deliberately fail terminally after tool execution or assistant output begins, rather than using the existing transient retry, to avoid duplicate partial side effects?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically focused, but it intentionally changes the recovery contract for already-active CLI work; the protected maintainer label indicates this tradeoff needs an explicit human decision.

options.title: Accept the no-replay safety boundary
options.body: Confirm that preventing duplicate side effects outweighs automatic recovery for transient failures after visible CLI activity begins.

options.title: Preserve an explicit recovery mode
options.body: Keep the compatibility retry behavior only behind a separately designed, documented policy if maintainers require it for existing workflows.

recommendation.title: Accept the no-replay safety boundary
recommendation.body: Confirm that preventing duplicate side effects outweighs automatic recovery for transient failures after visible CLI activity begins.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the live incident context and authored the proposed timeout/replay boundary.
